query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a protective coating of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance at high temperatures.
generation.conditions: High temperature (800 °C) in an oxidative atmosphere (air) for 5 hours.
generation.mechanism: The aluminum oxide coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, preventing oxidation of the underlying alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance compared to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, with reduced oxidation and pesting.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exposed to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable at 800 °C in air for a duration of 5 hours.
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the aluminum oxide coating specifically on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has not been previously established.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the oxidation behavior of coated and uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples after exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples show equal or greater weight gain and similar or worse mechanical properties compared to uncoated samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
